nodes.name: Pt NDs synthesis
nodes.procedure: 1 mL of H₂PtCl₆ aqueous solution (10×10⁻³ M) was mixed with 5 mL of C₂₂N·COOH (Br⁻) aqueous solution (10×10⁻³ M). Then, 0.5 mL of fresh AA aqueous solution (0.3×10⁻³ M) was injected into the above mixture rapidly followed by gentle shaking. The mixture was kept at 50°C for 4 h and cooled to room temperature.
nodes.source_text: H₂PtCl₆ aqueous solution (10×10⁻³ M,1 mL) was added and mixed with the C₂₂N·COOH (Br⁻) aqueous solution (10×10⁻³ M,5 mL). Then, 0.5 mL of fresh AA aqueous solution (0.3×10⁻³ M,1 mL) was injected... The mixture was kept at 25°C. After 4h...

nodes.name: P-doping of Pt NDs
nodes.procedure: After 4 h at 50°C, the mixture was cooled to room temperature. Then NaH₂PO₂ aqueous solution (10×10⁻³ M, 0.2 mL) was mixed into the above mixture. The reaction solution was kept at room temperature for another 4 h. Finally, the PtP NDs products were collected by centrifugation and washed several times with ethanol after removal of surfactants.
nodes.source_text: After 4h, NaH₂PO₂ aqueous solution (10×10⁻³ M,0.2 mL) was mixed into the above mixture. The reaction solution was kept at 50°C for another 4h. Finally, the PtP NDs products were collected by centrifugation...

unit_operations.name: Phosphating
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: NaH₂PO₂ aqueous solution (10×10⁻³ M,0.2 mL) was mixed into the above mixture. The reaction solution was kept at room temperature for another 4 h

unit_operations.name: Purification

nodes.name: Organic surfactant synthesis
nodes.procedure: 7.6 g of N,N-dimethyldocosylamine (20 mmol), 2.6 g of bromoacetic acid (22 mmol), and acetonitrile (150 mL) were refluxed under 95°C for 20 h. After the removal of the solvent, the crude product was washed with diethyl ether several times to remove the unreacted reactants and dried in a Freeze dryer.
nodes.source_text: Taking the synthesis of C_{22}N-COOH (Br^{-}) for an example, 7.6 g of N,N-dimethyldocosylamine (20 mmol), 2.6 g of bromoacetic acid (22 mmol), and acetonitrile (150 mL) were refluxed under 95°C for 20 h.

nodes.source_text: The result illustrated that the catalytic activity of PtP NDs was strongly dependent on the P content... PtP NDs with the best HER performance had a P doping of 0.84 at%.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images present a highly branched structure with no other impurities observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The low- and high-magnification transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images present a highly branched structure with no other impurities observed (Figure 2a,b).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM displays two distinct lattice fringes with d-spacing values of 1.96 and 2.25 Å ascribed to the (200) and (111) facets of typical face-centered cubic (fcc) crystal structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM (HRTEM) displays two distinct lattice fringes with d -spacing values of 1.96 and 2.25Å (Figure 2c and Figure S1, Supporting Information), ascribed to the (200) and (111) facets of typical face-centered cubic (fcc) crystal structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern shows no obvious shift of diffraction peaks compared to Pt NDs and unchanged FWHM, indicating P doping does not affect crystallinity and doping amount is extremely low.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with the wide-angle X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of Pt NDs, PtP NDs did not exhibit an obvious shift of diffraction peaks (Figure 2e). Additionally, the full width at half maxima (FWHM) of the diffraction peaks in PtP NDs remains unchanged...

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt 4f peaks at 71.6 and 74.9 eV for Pt⁰ with positive shift of ≈0.6 eV indicating charge transfer from Pt to P; extra peaks at 73.9 and 76.9 eV from Pt-P formation; P 2p negative shift at 129.2 eV confirming Pt-P bonds.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The core-level spectra of Pt 4f show two peaks at 71.6 and 74.9eV (Figure 2f)... Compared with pure Pt NDs, there are an extra set of peaks at 73.9 and 76.9eV, which come from the formation of Pt-P (Figure S3, Supporting Information). In the spectra of P 2p (Figure 2 g)... a negative shift is found in PtP NDs (129.2 eV), again indicating the formation of Pt-P bonds.

The elemental composition and ratio in PtP NDs are verified by inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-AES), which displays a very low amount of P almost at the atomic level (≈0.84 at%, Figure S4, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM image and EDS elemental mapping show P element uniformly distributed in PtP NDs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) image and corresponding EDS elemental mapping show that P element is uniformly distributed in PtP NDs (Figure 2 h).

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern confirms exposed (110) facets similar to Pt NDs, indicating P doping did not affect crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding fast Fourier transformation (FFT) (the inset in Figure 2c) and selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern (Figure S1d, Supporting Information) further confirm the exposed (110) facets in PtP NDs...

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping with HAADF-STEM shows uniform P distribution in PtP NDs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) image and corresponding EDS elemental mapping show that P element is uniformly distributed in PtP NDs (Figure 2 h).
